# Facebook (FB) Deep Dive Analysis

Report 035 | Published 2020-09-27 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2020-9-27/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/035.json)

Facebook value and a fiscal trading framework.

Facebook was a successful long-window selection and its conservative initial EPS growth was surpassed. The analysis usefully identified privacy sensitivity, but its assertion that buybacks had not begun was wrong. The comparison also underestimated Cadence growth. Fiscal timing and the proposed technical entry rule remain less auditable than the company forecast.

**Coverage:** All numbered text blocks and image labels read. Material theses, forecasts and explanations are included; routine holdings lists, incidental statistics, company descriptions and boilerplate are excluded. Chart pixels were not inspected.

## Claims

### 035-C01

**Inflation expectations govern risk assets**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | Cross-assets |
| Source blocks | 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 |
| Thesis family | breakeven-risk-asset-regime |

The 2020 co-movement is observable, and the author correctly notes chart-axis alignment exaggerates similarity. Common liquidity shocks can move both series; a two-axis chart does not establish inflation expectations as the independent cause.

**Direction:** See reason; no return inferred.

**Timing:** No fixed endpoint supplied.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Ten-year inflation compensation sensitivity](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DFII10) | Federal Reserve via FRED | Verified in the audit

DGS 10 minus DFII 10: August 31, 2020 1.80%, September 14 1.65%, September 25 1.58%, December 23 1.97%. Breakeven includes inflation-risk and liquidity premia, not pure expected CPI.

- [Autumn 2020 correction](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SP500) | S&P Dow Jones Indices via FRED | Verified in the audit

S&P 500 closes August 24 3431.28, September 2 3580.84, September 23 3236.92, December 24 3703.06. September peak-to-trough close decline approximately 9.60%, followed by new highs. Excludes dividends.

- [June 2020 Monetary Policy Report, part 2](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/2020-06-mpr-part2.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2020-06-12 | Verified in the audit

Investors sold longer Treasuries and MBS for liquid assets; Treasury bid-ask spreads widened and dealer balance-sheet constraints impaired intermediation. Purchases and lending aimed to restore market function.

**Outcome evidence:**

Personal income fell 4.2% in May after revised 10.8% growth in April. Declining recovery payments explained much of the decrease, partly offset by unemployment benefits. Spending rose 8.2%.

The subsequent broad relief act passed Congress December 21 and was signed December 27, 2020, after the election rather than during summer.

Contemporary estimate: Q3 2020 real GDP +33.4% annualized, Q4 +4.1%. There was no renewed quarterly contraction in the second half of 2020.

The release reported payroll employment and unemployment rate had returned to February 2020 levels in July 2022. This is a publication-vintage recovery date, not a claim about subsequently revised payroll history.

The company repurchased 4.202 bn of stock in 2019, before the article. It had not yet initiated a dividend, but grouping dividends and repurchases into a never-returned-capital claim is incorrect.
